result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.disjoint_union()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the disjoint union of this graph with another graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12372-L12448){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.disjoint_union(other) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Combines graphs by renumbering the other graph's nodes to avoid conflicts. The resulting graph has all nodes and edges from both, with no overlap. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The graph to combine with (its nodes will be renumbered). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with both graphs combined disjointly. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graphs have different directedness. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - The other graph's nodes are renumbered starting after this graph's max ID - Labels are preserved but IDs change - Use regular `union()` if you want to merge overlapping node IDs ## Examples {.doc-examples} Unlike `union()`, node IDs are never merged here -- even though both graphs use IDs `1`, `2`, `3`, the second graph's nodes are renumbered so the two triangles stay completely separate: ::: {#28a20bd9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Two separate triangles t1 = ec.Graph(directed=False) for i in range(1, 4): t1.add_node() t1.add_edge(1, 2) t1.add_edge(2, 3) t1.add_edge(3, 1) t2 = ec.Graph(directed=False) for i in range(1, 4): t2.add_node() t2.add_edge(1, 2) t2.add_edge(2, 3) t2.add_edge(3, 1) combined = t1.disjoint_union(t2) combined.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 6 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#dbece79a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} combined.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 6 ``` ::: ::: Chaining several calls together is a quick way to build a graph out of multiple independent components: ::: {#427ec41c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} component1 = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(5) component2 = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(6) component3 = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(4) multi = component1.disjoint_union(component2).disjoint_union(component3) multi.count_weakly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 3 ``` ::: :::
